newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police seize over 10,000 kg of hashish.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police seize over 10,000 kg of hashish.

text.p: Sri Lankan police have seized more than 10,000 kilograms (10 tonnes) of hashish this week and may be on the trail of an international drug smuggling operation, police anti-narcotics officials said on Wednesday.

Authorities on Tuesday detected 158 kg (348 pounds) of the drug from a house in Madampe, 60 km (35 miles) north of the capital Colombo, senior superintendent of police of the Anti-Narcotics Division, C.L. Ratnayake, told Reuters.
On Sunday, police siezed another 10,150 kg (10.15 tonnes) of hashish as it was being unloaded from a trawler off the coast of the same area, Ratnayake said.
"We believe the stuff originated from Afghanistan and was in transit to some other country. Hashish has no big demand in this country," he said.

Anti-narcotics officials said hashish is a potent resinous byproduct of cannabis and is produced mostly in India, Pakistan and Afghanistan. In Sri Lanka, it has a street value of about 40,000 rupees ($700) per kilo, they said.
Officials said the Indian Ocean island may be used by international dealers as a distribution point for hashish bound for European countries.
The last time a major quantity of hashish was detected in Sri Lanka was in 1990 when police seized 52 kg (114.4 pouns) from the same area, Ratnayake said.
